Uśanas-nīti
Mithilā. For Uśanas q.s on Nīti, see Kane, HDS. I. p. 110; also under Śukranīti.

Uśanah2smṛti,_U._Dharmaśāstra,_Auśanasasmṛti,_Au._Dha._Śā.
Current in three texts, one in prose in 7 chs. interspersed with verses; an. two in verses, one short version in 51 verses, an. another, long, in 9 chs. Some of the verses in the prose text occur in the metrical texts too; of Uśanas q.s in many Smṛtis an. Nibandhas, in prose an. verse, some are found in the above three texts, an. some in none. See Kane, HDS. I. p.. 110-6.

Text ptd. in Dutt's Dharma Sastra Texts, Vol. I. p.. 111-164 in 9 chs. an. called U. saṁhitā; also Jīvānanda's D.. śāstrasaṅgraha, Calcutta 1876; Eng. transl. by same editor, Calcutta 1906, Vol. I. p.. 189-267. Most of the mss. go only upto part of ch. V. of the above ptd. text. Burnell 124b (3 mss. 9 chs.; one 4 chs. only).

Uśanasādbhutāni
73rd Atharvapariśiṣṭa. Weber 366 (73).
71st of Pt.. text. See Auśanasādbhutāni.

Uṣah2pānīya
med. on drinking water in the morning.

Uṣāniruddha
Pkt. kāvya in 4 cantos. by Rāma Pāṇivāda.

Ed.. (1) J. of the Bomb. Uni. X. ii. 1941, p.. 156-194. (2) Adyar Library, 42. 1943, with chāyā. The Adyar edn. used another ms. in private posession of one of its editors.

Uṣāniruddhacarita
mentioned in the list of works of Kumāratātācārya (Śrīśaila Śatakratu etc.) an. his sons in his son's Kumāratātayārya-vaibhavaprakāśikā, ptd. Grantha script, Kumbhakonam, p. 4, śl. 48.

Uṣāniruddhanāṭaka
by a king of Kāśī named Lakṣmīnātha. Rep. Raj. & C. I. p. 52.

Uṣāniruddhīya
kāvya in 9 cantos. by Viśvanātha (Col. Digubbapadavīraṭa-Viśvanātha ?).

Uṣāpariṇaya
campū. by Kṛṣṇa Kavi. Oppert

Uṣāpariṇaya
campū, prabandha. by Ilayiḍattu Nārāyaṇa Nambūdri (?) (1770-1840 A. D.); but a.. in mss. entries. Āmpallūr 7. Kizhakkumbhāgattu Mana 44.

Uṣāpariṇaya
a drama in 7 acts, by Guṇḍu Rāmasvāmi Śāstrī, son of Rāmabrahma. [Page401-b]
Pt.. Velangi, Cocanada, 1910. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1906-28. 868.

Uṣāpariṇaya
nāṭaka. by Śrīnivāsācārya. Rice 256. C.. the entry before the previous.

Uṣābhilāṣa
a musical poem intended for dance a. the festival in Pūri. by Nārāyaṇa of 18th century. See V. Raghavan, Bhoja's Śṛṅgāra Prakāśa, 1963, p. 551; also J. of the Madras Music Academy, IV. p. 76.

Uṣābhilāṣa
kāvya. (1555 A. D.). by Śiśuśaṅkara. similar to Gītagovinda.
See Proceed. AIOC. XVIII. Annamalainagar, 1955. p. 176.

Uṣārāgodaya
nāṭikā. in 4 Acts. by Rudracandradeva. Alph. List Beng. Govt. p. 18 (2 mss.).

Uṣāharaṇa
by Veṅkaṭeśvaramakhin. ref. to by Veṅkaṭasubrahmaṇya, of a.'s family in the prologue to his Vasulakṣmīkalyāṇa

Uṣāharaṇa
kāvya cited by Bhoja in his Śṛ. Pra., a. having in the last verse of each canto the word ‘jaya’. See V. Raghavan, Bhoja's Śṛṅgāra Prakāśa, 1963, p. 706.
